stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, line \(\ell\) passes through the points \((2, 3)\) and \((6, 11)\). Line \(m\) is the reflection of line \(\ell\) across the line \(y = x\). What is the slope of line \(m\)?
solution: Reflecting a point across \(y = x\) swaps its coordinates: \((2, 3) \to (3, 2)\) and \((6, 11) \to (11, 6)\).
Slope of \(m\): \(\frac{6 - 2}{11 - 3} = \frac{1}{2}\) (the reciprocal of the slope of \(\ell\), which is 2).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(-2\) is the slope of a line perpendicular to \(\ell\); reflection across \(y = x\) gives the reciprocal, not the negative reciprocal.
explanation.B: Correct. Reflecting across \(y = x\) swaps coordinates: \(m\) passes through \((3, 2)\) and \((11, 6)\), so its slope is \(\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. The reflected line still rises from left to right, since both points keep positive coordinates in the same order.
explanation.D: Incorrect. 2 is the slope of \(\ell\) itself; reflecting across \(y = x\) changes the slope to its reciprocal.

verify:
m = Rational(6 - 2, 11 - 3)
assert m == Rational(1, 2) and m == 1/Rational(11 - 3, 6 - 2)
assert value(choices[answer]) == m
assert all(value(choices[k]) != m for k in choices if k != answer)
